content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have an old [product_name] ([article_no]). It's already programmed and in use. When I supply power, the display shows three lines: PC<-->[product_name], STOP Press ESC. When I press ESC, the device runs, but I can't return to programming mode afterwards. Also, pressing ESC again does nothing.
Hi, while running, try pressing Button Right, Button Left, and OK simultaneously.

Hello, is the cable connected? If so, disconnect the cable and try again. If the [product_name] is in RUN mode and you perform a power cycle, it should start running unless it was in STOP or the cable was connected. Hope this helps.
I'm experiencing the same issue whether the cable is connected or not. When powering on, the [product_name] is in STOP, and pressing ESC makes it run and remain in RUN mode.

Hi, if the programming cable is connected and power is turned on, the [product_name] will switch to PC --> [product_name] mode regardless of whether it was previously in RUN mode. This is documented in the [document] for [article_no] on page 119. To solve, disconnect the cable and power it on. To change to RUN when the display shows PC --> [product_name], press the cursor down to START. To switch the device back to transfer mode, press the left cursor, right cursor, and OK buttons simultaneously. You can find further details in the [document] for [article_no] page 32 or page 40 of the PDF. The manual is available online; just scroll down and select 'technical documentation.' Hope this helps.
This FAQ was posted on the [company_name] support site the same day I asked my question: [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Users report challenges returning to programming mode on an older [product_name] ([article_no]) after exiting STOP mode by pressing ESC. Pressing ESC during RUN mode does not return to the previous state, which feels nonintuitive. Solutions involving pressing multiple keys simultaneously or disconnecting cables are not obvious, indicating low discoverability and limited ease of use for those less familiar with the product.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that pressing ESC or a similarly accessible button will enable easy switching between RUN and programming or STOP modes on the device.
